history.summary: The 'Ashtashambhu' of this CSV row is the group of EIGHT Shiva temples of the Bargarh-Sambalpur region of western Odisha, listed on the Bargarh tourism page as 'Astasambhu Temple, Bargarh' with the address Astasambhu Temple, Bargarh Rd, Bardol, Bargarh, Odisha 768038 (hence the CSV town 'Bargarh'). The eight pithas are: Bimaleswar at Huma, Nilakantheswar at Nilji, Kedarnath at Ambabhona, Bisweswar at Soranda, Baidyanath at Deogaon, Swapneswar at Sorna, Mandhata Baba at Maneswar, and Balunkeswar at Gaisama. They were built under the Chauhan kings of Sambalpur; one of them, the Swapneswar temple at Sorna, is documented as built by Raja Ajit Singh Dev in 1725-1776. A local Astashambhu Yatra visits the circuit. MAJOR AMBIGUITY FLAG: the batch brief states '788 Ashtashambhu is at Kualo, Sambalpur district'. No source supports 'Kualo, Sambalpur': the documented Ashtashambhu Temple at Kualo is in Parajang, Dhenkanal district (an 8-shrine Shaiva complex of the Sulki/Stambha dynasty, 9th century, per IGNCA/ASI records) - a DIFFERENT site ~180 km away. Reviewer decision needed: keep this file as the western-Odisha Chauhan circuit (matching the CSV town Bargarh), or repurpose the row for the Kualo (Dhenkanal) temples.
